article.dek: It is game day in Baltimore: an undrafted rookie makes his first start under the lights, the inactive list is the last check before kickoff, and the Thursday line has settled with Jacksonville near a 10-point favorite.

items.headline: Lead: Game day in Baltimore, and the rookie starts
paragraphs: It is game day. Jacksonville visits Baltimore tonight, Thursday, November 5, at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. The Jaguars are 5-2. The Ravens are 4-4 and have lost three straight.

Baltimore's quarterback is settled, and it is the story of the night. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano makes his first career start. Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve after right thumb surgery, and Tyler Huntley is out for the season with a turf toe injury that needs surgery. Fagnano came on in relief last Sunday at Buffalo and went 10 of 21 for 91 yards with an interception. He is dealing with an ankle issue of his own, but he was a full participant in Tuesday's practice and head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Tuesday that Fagnano starts. Kedon Slovis, signed off Green Bay's practice squad, backs him up.

The trade headline does not change tonight. Baltimore is finalizing a deal for veteran Jacoby Brissett, but it is not expected to be completed until the weekend, so Brissett would debut Monday, November 16, against the Los Angeles Chargers. Tonight belongs to Fagnano. The inactive list lands about 90 minutes before kickoff, and that is the last check before you act on a Thursday price.
items.takeaway: Tonight is Jacksonville at Baltimore at 8:15 p.m. ET; Fagnano makes his first start, and Brissett is a next-week story, not a Thursday one.

items.headline: Injury roundup: final designations stand — Tuten and Walker are game-time calls
paragraphs: Nothing new arrived overnight. The final designations from Wednesday still stand, and the inactive list about 90 minutes before kickoff is what settles the two game-time calls.

For Jacksonville, running back Bhayshul Tuten is questionable and a game-time decision after missing all week with ankle and foot injuries. Defensive end Travon Walker is questionable with a rib injury after limited practices Tuesday and Wednesday. Wide receiver Jakobi Meyers, running back Chris Rodriguez Jr., guard Ezra Cleveland, and safety Antonio Johnson carry no game status and are good to go. Defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton and safety Eric Murray are out for the season.

For Baltimore, rookie guard Vega Ioane carries no designation and is set to return after missing one game with a knee injury. Cornerback Nate Wiggins is questionable after missing Wednesday's practice with an illness. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins misses a third straight game with a knee injury. Kicker Tyler Loop is on injured reserve with a groin injury, so Jake Moody is expected to kick tonight.
items.takeaway: Tuten and Walker are game-time decisions; Ioane is clear, Wiggins is questionable with an illness, and Hawkins is out.

items.headline: Weather: mild in Baltimore at kickoff, rain chances rise through the evening
paragraphs: Thursday night in Baltimore looks mild with rain in the picture. The forecast for M&T Bank Stadium calls for temperatures in the high 60s at kickoff, falling into the mid-60s through the evening, with a chance of rain showers that rises as the night goes on. Wind is light, out of the south at just a few miles per hour around kickoff.

That is a factual weather read, not a totals edge. Mostly dry conditions are expected around the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, with an isolated shower or thunderstorm possible during the game. If you are going, pack for rain. If you are betting, do not turn a rain chance into a totals opinion on its own.
items.takeaway: Thursday night in Baltimore: high 60s at kickoff, light south wind, and a rising chance of rain showers through the evening.

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — no Thursday cards yet, so Thursday goes through Check
paragraphs: The morning board is the same board as last night. Read after the refresh window Thursday morning, it still shows Week 8, generated November 2, with no Week 9 cards at all. Its Baltimore game is still the Week 8 trip to Buffalo, and its quarterback field is blank — it has not picked up Fagnano as tonight's starter.

The only cards on it are Monday's history, and they are worth one look because they show how the three cards differ. On Chicago at Seattle, the Value card and the Balanced card were the same play: Chicago +3 at -102, with the model giving Chicago a 50.6% chance against a market price implying 46.5% — a +3.6% edge. The Hit Rate card was Seattle on the moneyline at -175, with the model at 56.1% against a market price implying 60.4% — a negative edge, because Hit Rate forgoes value for win probability. Hit Rate is the pick most likely to win. Balanced is a strong pick without paying too much, a good starting point for a new bettor. Value is always the model's +EV play. None of them is deficient for being a different kind of pick.

So there are no Thursday cards to read this morning, and you should not force a pick out of a stale board. That is what Check is for. If your book already has a Thursday line, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: Board still shows Week 8 with no Week 9 cards, so Thursday's price goes through Check until the board flips.

items.headline: Learn the Game: closing line value — beating the number that matters
paragraphs: Closing line value, usually shortened to CLV, is a simple idea. It asks whether the price you took was better than the price available right before the game started. If you bet a team at -3 and the line closes at -5, you got closing line value. If you bet it at -7 and it closes at -5, you did not.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say you take the Jaguars at -7 on Monday, and by Thursday night the line has moved to Jacksonville -9.5. You hold a better number than the closing line. That does not guarantee the bet wins. It means you paid less for the same side than the market ended up charging.

Why it matters: over a long run, bettors who regularly beat the closing line tend to be on the right side of the market more often than bettors who do not. One game proves nothing. The habit, measured over many bets, is the signal.
items.takeaway: Closing line value means you took a better price than the closing line; it does not guarantee a win, but beating the close over many bets is a good sign.

items.headline: Thursday's line has settled with Jacksonville near 10, and the total has ticked down to 39.5
paragraphs: The Thursday line has barely moved since last night, and the total has inched down. Jacksonville is -9.5 at -120 on FanDuel, with Baltimore +10 at -109 on BetRivers. The moneyline is Jacksonville -500 and Baltimore +425. The total is 39.5, over -105 on Fanatics and under -105 on Hard Rock Bet. That is down from 40.5 last night.

Step back and the move is still the quarterback news. A week ago the lookahead had Baltimore as a 3-point favorite with a total of 48.5. Jackson's thumb injury, Huntley's season-ending turf toe, and Fagnano's first start flipped the favorite and pulled the total down about nine points. The market has now settled around Jacksonville by 10 with a total near 40.

The app has not caught any of it yet. The board still shows Week 8, generated November 2, so none of these Thursday prices are on a card. If your book has a Thursday line you like, run it through Check: type in the line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator for a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: From Baltimore -3 and a 48.5 total a week ago to Jacksonville -9.5 and a 39.5 total now — the quarterback news moved it, and it has settled.

items.headline: Thursday game? Thursday check — and bet the good number now
paragraphs: If your book has a Thursday number you like, run it through Check now and, if Check says bet, bet it now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number later, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too. The one thing still worth waiting on is the inactive list, about 90 minutes before kickoff — if Tuten, Walker, or Wiggins changes status there, run your price through Check again before you act.
One housekeeping note: settlement in the app is manual, and the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself. Log the losers too. A record that only keeps the wins is not a record.
items.takeaway: Run your book's Thursday price through Check now; if it says bet, bet the good number now — and log the result either way, win or lose.
